body: CI error looks like a pretty nasty include order problem. Anyone got ideas?

> CI error looks like a pretty nasty include order problem. Anyone got ideas?

Tried something after checking where `VOID` is defined in mingw/windows headers. I can't reproduce the issue locally (at least running only the command to compile that one file) on Fedora 42, but I have newer mingw headers than the CI runner, so maybe the issue was fixed already upstream.

*Edit:* Didn't work, I'll try to reproduce this on the `ubuntu:24.04` docker image tomorrow.

Pre-processed source to the rescue (160,000 lines of code...), the problem is that `GDScriptTokenizer::Token` defines a `VOID` enum, and for that has `#undef VOID`. With the change in includes ordering `mutex.h` and `mingw-std-threads` get included after this code, so `VOID` isn't defined anymore.

These `#undef`s were added by @RandomShaper in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/85039/files#diff-b228a56a94f75a6524d89e12049b0ccde498caa71fedbec5b98fa37fbeef844e and I was already wary of them at the time. We now have the confirmation that they're not the proper solution.

> Simplify StringName to bool conversions. If _data is set, _data->name is guaranteed to be not empty. This speeds up the function considerably, and decreases the binary size by 0.6mb.

From my testing, this PR actually makes a Linux x86_64 release export template binary size (with LTO) a bit larger:

- `master`: 70,426,536 bytes
- This PR: 70,614,984 bytes

I've done a full clean build (cleared all caches, including ccache) and can still reproduce this difference.

> > Simplify StringName to bool conversions. If _data is set, _data->name is guaranteed to be not empty. This speeds up the function considerably, and decreases the binary size by 0.6mb.
>

Funny that 😄
As is often the case when making a common function inlineable, we get chaotic effects; some compilers use it to gain space and others to optimize and unroll surrounding calls for performance gains 😅

Comparing file sizes from [this PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/14719431783) vs [master](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/14736446766), it looks like the changes are all over the place (again). Hard to take anything from that, beyond compilers doing their thing!
Now that #105897 is merged, this should be good to go after a rebase

> Now that https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105897 is merged, this should be good to go after a rebase

Looks like that's the case, tests are passing now.

Thanks a lot @akien-mga!
